newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was uneven this week on light demand and light to moderate offerings, USDA said.
Retail and HRI demand was fairly light for immediate needs, while improved forward interest was noted, especially on the end cuts. Choice middle meats traded sharply higher on light offerings.
Select middle meats tried to follow suit with the Choice, but with the abundance of Select product, packers were forced to control inventories and these cuts struggled to maintain steady levels.
Chuck and round cuts traded steady to firm with most of the advances early in the week on the Choice product, while Select cuts ended the trading period on a weak undertone.

Closely trimmed items traded uneven on light to moderate demand with Choice cuts trending higher and Select product trading generally steady as these cuts were more abundant. Beef trimmings traded at steady levels early in the week, but as the week progressed and slaughter levels remained high, trade on beef trimmings lowered on light to moderate demand and mostly moderate offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings; however, a weak undertone was noted on the blended coarse ground items.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.00 to 6.50 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to 3.00; Select and Choice round primal steady to 2.50 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 7.00 higher; Closely trimmed items steady to 3.50 higher; Beef trimmings 1.50 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up $3.02 at $114.28; 700/850 Up $3.29 at $112.48; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up $0.46 at $99.66; 700/850 Dn $0.45 at $98.25.
